findings.description: The MySQL parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections, allowing credentials and catalog data to traverse the VPC in cleartext.

The instance user_data embeds the RDS master username and the password variable (var.password) in cleartext inside a shell heredoc. EC2 user data is retrievable in plaintext from the instance metadata service (and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute), so any SSRF or local access on the host discloses the database master credentials. It is also stored unencrypted in Terraform state.

No root_block_device/ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the instance's EBS volumes may be created unencrypted, leaving the credential file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) and application data at rest without encryption.

metadata_options is not set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with the instance profile aws_iam_instance_profile.catalog_app_profile and a PHP application that processes user input, an SSRF flaw could retrieve the role's temporary credentials from the metadata endpoint.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the application over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration, so form-submitted personal data (names and addresses) and responses travel unencrypted.

The generated PHP connects to RDS with mysqli_connect() without any SSL/TLS options or certificate verification, so credentials and query data traverse the network in cleartext between the app server and the database.
The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database storage and snapshots hold catalog data in cleartext, with no KMS protection against disk- or snapshot-level exposure.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database directly to untrusted networks and relying solely on the security group and credentials for protection.

The master password is taken from var.password and the username is the predictable default 'admin'; the password is passed in plaintext through Terraform variables and stored in cleartext in Terraform state rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or managed via manage_master_user_password.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Because this role is attached via the instance profile to the internet-facing catalog_app_server, compromise of that instance yields full control over all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including a privilege-escalation path through EC2 and RDS modification.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data-exfiltration and command-and-control channel from a compromised database host.

Ingress on port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than from the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database; combined with publicly_accessible = true this rule is the only remaining network control.

Nothing in the configuration forces TLS for client connections (no require_secure_transport enforcement referenced here), so MySQL traffic to a publicly reachable endpoint may traverse the network unencrypted.
